what_it_does: Diffusion models generate images by repeatedly denoising a picture over dozens or hundreds of steps, which is slow and energy-hungry. SQ-DM attacks this cost two ways at once: it rounds every number in the model down to just 4 bits (one quarter of the usual 32-bit precision), and it also skips computing neurons whose output would be near zero anyway (a technique called activation sparsity, because most activations are sparse — close to zero — at any given moment). The tricky part is that which neurons are near zero changes not only from image region to image region but also from denoising step to step, making the pattern unpredictable. The paper designs a custom chip that handles mixed precision (some operations in 4 bits, some in more bits) and detects on the fly which activations can be skipped at each step, so it only does the math that truly matters.
